hypotheses.justification: hC follows from hFC. Since ℝ is nonempty, 0 ≤ ‖F 0‖ ≤ C, which is `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hFC 0)`. In the proof, hC is only passed to the inner lemma, and there it is only used to get `0 ≤ B`. Replace it with this derived fact. Deleting hC leaves the statement true and provable.

The statement stays true for T < 0. In that case `Set.uIoc 0 T = Ioc T 0`, so every τ in it has τ ≤ 0. The integrand `mildShiftedStokesIntegrand F t τ` is 0 whenever ¬(0 < τ), so the interval integral is 0 for every t. The function is then constant and continuous. A proof splits on `0 ≤ T`. The case `0 ≤ T` is the existing proof. The case T < 0 uses `intervalIntegral.integral_congr` to rewrite the integrand to 0 on `uIoc`, and then `integral_zero` gives a constant function. In the existing proof, hT is used only for `Set.uIoc_of_le hT`. Only the dominated-convergence bound needs hT, because `τ^(-1/2)` can be negative for τ < 0. This hypothesis can be deleted on its own, independently of hC.
